title: A Model for Teaching Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Research Computing to Domain Scientists on HPC Resources
problem: Domain scientists (biologists) lack HPC, machine learning, and deep learning skills; traditional training models ineffective for domain scientists unfamiliar with command-line computing and HPC systems.
motivation: Effective HPC education requires hands-on, accessible training on real systems. Domain scientists need ML/DL knowledge to leverage HPC for biological discovery, but traditional HPC training assumes CS background.
method: One-week workshop teaching biologists: command-line file systems (basics), SLURM job submission, machine learning and deep learning techniques applied to real biological datasets. Delivery via Jupyter Notebooks, graphical interfaces (DCV), software containers on HPC with minimal setup.
key_novelty: Adaptable workshop framework for teaching domain scientists HPC/ML/DL using accessible technologies (notebooks, GUI, containers); demonstrated effectiveness via survey data.
contributions: Workshop model for teaching HPC/ML/DL to domain scientists
limitations: Limited detail on survey metrics (pre/post improvement quantification)
Workshop scalability and long-term retention unclear
No comparison with other educational approaches
Biological dataset diversity and relevance not specified
primary_theme: Accessible HPC/ML/DL education for domain scientists
